statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the maximum of the set of all sums sum_{k=i}^{j} nums[k] such that 0 <= i <= j < n and, for every k with i <= k < j, nums[k] < nums[k+1]. The set is nonempty because every singleton i = j is allowed, so the maximum is well defined; in particular the function does not fail.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= sum_{k=0}^{n-1} nums[k].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i <= j < n and for every k with i <= k < j, nums[k] < nums[k+1], we have sum_{k=i}^{j} nums[k] <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist i and j with 0 <= i <= j < n such that, for every k with i <= k < j, nums[k] < nums[k+1], and sum_{k=i}^{j} nums[k] = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = nums[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n = 1 and 1 <= nums[0] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} nums[k].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, nums[i] < nums[i+1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max_{0 <= i < n} nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, nums[i] >= nums[i+1].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the maximum of the set of sums sum_{k=l}^{t} nums[k] over all intervals [l,t] with 0 <= l <= t < n that satisfy all three conditions: (i) for every k with l <= k < t, nums[k] < nums[k+1]; (ii) l = 0 or nums[l-1] >= nums[l]; (iii) t = n-1 or nums[t] >= nums[t+1]. These intervals are exactly the maximal strictly increasing contiguous runs.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = if nums[0] < nums[1] then nums[0] + nums[1] else max(nums[0], nums[1]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n = 2, 1 <= nums[0] <= 100, and 1 <= nums[1] <= 100.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every p with 0 <= p < n-1 and nums[p] >= nums[p+1], the following holds: r = max(Best(0,p), Best(p+1,n-1)), where for any 0 <= a <= b < n, Best(a,b) is defined as the maximum of the set of sums sum_{k=i}^{j} nums[k] such that a <= i <= j <= b and, for every k with i <= k < j, nums[k] < nums[k+1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n >= 1 and n <= 100, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 100.
